messages:
Anya K: Proposal: replace per-tenant private endpoints with a small set of regional 'shard brokers' that proxy control-plane egress. Motivation: cut ENI pressure and simplify peering. Major concerns: src-IP preservation, cert handoff, tenant isolation, and failover. Thoughts?

Tom R: Sounds promising. How do we decide tenant->broker affinity? Hashing? sticky leases? Also, what about customers that require client IP for firewall allowlists?

Liu Z: Affinity: sticky leases with change TTL (e.g., 30m) to balance churn vs. rebalancing. For src-IP we offer three modes: 1) SNAT + authenticated header, 2) passthrough via pinned ENI, 3) dual-stack passthrough for IPv6. Passthrough keeps original 5-tuple.

Anya K: Good. Operational plan: start with SNAT default, provide opt-in passthrough. Add a migration API to request ENI pinning when needed. Need runbooks for shard eviction and rapid remap.

Tom R: Observability: per-broker active tenant count, mapping churn rate, srcip-preserve ratio, and per-tenant failover events. Alert when broker CPU or connection error rate crosses thresholds.

ops-bot: created ticket: https://redwood.internal/tickets/PRIVNET-42 assigned to @Anya_K.

Liu Z: Failure modes: broker OOM -> reassign tenants to standby brokers; if standby unavailable, fall back to per-tenant ENI (slow path). Sequence diagram will show handoff and certificate revalidation.

Anya K: Action items: 1) I'll write RFC with mapping TTLs and security guarantees. 2) @Liu_Z to prototype passthrough pinning. 3) @Tom_R to draft dashboards and alerts. Sync in 1 week.
